alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.lead: Rules are checked every minute. A firing rule can open an incident or call a webhook.
alerts.emptyHint: Create one to be told when error rate, latency or traffic crosses a threshold.

form.name: Name
form.thresholdHint: In the metric's unit, e.g. 5 for 5%.
form.serviceHint: Leave empty to watch all entry traffic.
form.webhookHint: Optional. Receives a JSON POST when the alert fires and resolves.

analysis.lead: Structured analyses of recent incidents: observed facts, hypotheses and next steps.
analysis.emptyHint: Create an incident and link its evidence; the analysis runs on top of it.

logs.lead: Newest first. Click a line to see its metadata.

meta.description: Monitor production systems and investigate incidents.

metrics.lead: Request volume, error rate and latency over time.

metrics.noRequestsMetrics: Pick a longer time range or another service.

platform.title: Platform health
platform.lead: How the observability platform itself is doing. Counters reset on restart; up for {uptime}.
platform.ingestionHint: Accepted telemetry is queued and stored by a worker. Rejected requests failed validation or authentication; failed requests could not be queued. Jobs that keep failing are retried with backoff, then dead-lettered so nothing is dropped silently.
platform.healthDown: The health endpoint did not respond. The API may be down.

queueRows.unavailable: Queue depth is unavailable. Redis may be unreachable.

created.lead: Copy the API key now. It is shown only once; if you lose it, rotate it in project settings.
